newsitem.title: UK: Panamax rates advance on broad front.
newsitem.headline: Panamax rates advance on broad front.

text.p: Despite holidays in Japan and Taiwan, rates for modern Panamaxes on all BFI routes have continued to move ahead, brokers said.

They propelled the index up another 10 points on Thursday to 1054, a 54 point increase for the month so far. Cape sizes were described as "a little brighter". Handies were mixed but still strong for Lakes business and getting stronger from US Gulf.

GRAIN - Continental paid a sizeable premium to cover 50,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Aqaba for Oct 16/19 - Ascension was fixed at $18.50 basis 7,000 discharge compared to the fixture of Full Strong two weeks ago at $15.50 option 3,000 discharge at $17.00.

Rumours circulated of US Gulf/Continent fixed at $10.50 basis light grain. Hanjin were reported to have booked the Cosco vessel Full Comfort for 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for Nov 13/23 at $20.50 no combo, and it was believed that $21.00 had been bid this morning for the early Nov position (compared to last fixed for these dates of $20.00 by MOSK earlier this week).

Brokers reported that few vessels were in ballast in the Atlantic to US or Canadian loading ports and of course the supply of ballasting tonnage into the US Gulf from the East has now dried up completely.
In fact further increases in Panamax levels were seen in the North Pacific - a firmer $11.30 no combo has been agreed for 54,000 heavy grain Nopac/Japan for end Oct, possibly Dreyfus.
The Pakistan grain tender from Nopac was said to have been awarded on the basis of 3 shipments to Pan Ocean and one each to Kingston Maritime and Tristar.

But Navarino 63,880 dwt was confirmed fully fixed by Gemstar with grain for Oct 20/30 loading NoPac/Pakistan at $7,500 daily plus $150,000 bonus. A few days ago Amalia del Bene 64,221 dwt was fixed Nopac/china by Noble for similar dates at d6,500 daily plus d120,000 bonus.

In the handy market brokers said there were rumours of firmer rates agreed by charterers from the St Lawrence and by CAM from US Gulf to Algeria (possibly Alexandria for 25,000 tonnes at $18.00.) Brokers reported a build-up of grain enquiry from both North and South America.

MINERALS etc - KWK Legacy 149,000 dwt was fixed by Shinwa delivery prompt UK for a coal trip via Hampton Roads and Richards Bay to Japan at between $15,000 and $15,250 daily as a replacement for Baron Bay delayed at Narvik.

Mega Brook 123,000 dwt is believed fixed with ironore from Seven Islands to Antwerp and Grant were linked with a couple of 100/120,000 tonnes ironore lots from Goa to Taranto pier 2 for Dec/Jan, but full details were lacking.

Some potentially stronger Panamax fixtures in minerals were reported in the east on subjects: Showa have agreed $8,250 daily for Nordbulk 65,000 dwt delivery China Oct 20/30 for 2 laden legs Pacific business, and other Japanese charterers were believed to be involved in fixing modern Panamax tonnage for Australian coal trading at similar or firmer levels.

K line took Chungjin 69,634 dwt delivery Cigading for a trip via Australia to Japan at $8,100 daily. In the Atlantic Petra 64,848 dwt was understood fixed prompt Continent on subjects for a trip to the far East and Argolis 64,911 dwt was reported from New york to have been fixed by Samsun US Gulf/far East at about $9,500 daily plus $130,000 bonus.
Elli B 61,632 dwt was covered on private terms for short period, rumoured to be a profit-sharing deal with Kingston Maritime.

HANDYIZES - Brokers reported continued good demand for Laker tonnage. Pacific Carriers were understood to have fixed a vessel of about 30,000/35,000 dwt Continent/far East at between $10,000 and $10,500 daily, but conditions for Handymaxes on the Continent appeared to be quiet.

Tai Kang Hai 37,000 dwt open Boulogne Oct 17 was said to be on subjects for Atlantic business while in a far East market affected by holidays Furness Withy reportedly fixed Anangel Success 41,502 dwt for a trip via Australia to the Continent on private terms.
